simple.meaning: שׁוּעָל (shûwʻâl) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a jackal (as a burrower ).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 15:4. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship, prophetic witness, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שׁוּעָל (H7776) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שׁוּעָל (shûwʻâl) / H7776 is traced through Judges 15:4, Nehemiah 3:35, Psalms 63:11, Song of Songs 2:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H7776. shual I. שׁוּעָל noun masculine Song of Solomon 2:15 fox , perhaps also jackal ; — absolute ׳שׁ Neh 3:25 ; plural שׁוּעָלִים Judg 15:4 +, ׳שֻׁ Ezek 13:4 ; Song 2:15 b; — fox (probably) Neh 3:25 ; Song 2:15 (twice in verse); perhaps (from large number) jackal Judg 15:4 ; as haunting ruins Ezek 13:4 ; Lam 5:18 ; eating offal Psa 63:11 .
definitions.rootNote: or שֻׁעָל ; from the same as 8168 ;

occurrences.englishText: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the middle between every two tails.
But the king shall rejoice in God.
For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate.
Israel, your prophets have been like foxes in the waste places.
